about: Sister Ilse's own portrait (docs/cast/ilse.md): the regions of her sprite the pipeline works in, in the turned sprite's pixels (1024x1536), and the words for each mood and each mood's blink and talk. portrait.py reads it.
sprite: the sprite drawn on white by Qwen-Image-Edit from her design sheet (seed 1 of six), her hands folded at her waist, drawn facing left and turned by the cut (kept outside the repository, like every draft)
sheet: the expression sheet from the user's online model, twelve faces in four columns and three rows; `moodRefs` are its cells
keepWhy: the face, the veil and the white hair: nothing there is dark hair's edge
keepAlso: her eyebrows exactly as they are, faint and half under the bangs, with no new eyebrows or lines drawn above the eyes, the veil and its gold ornament
browsWhy: her thin, faint brows, half under the bangs, with room above for raised ones: a mood that moves them redraws all of it, so the old line goes

moods.happy: happy, gracefully: a gentle, warm closed-mouth smile, the corners of the lips softly raised, the lips closed (unlike picture 2's open mouth), the eyes closed in soft upward crescents as in picture 2
moods.sad: sad: the eyes lowered and a little glistening, the upper lids heavy, the lips closed in a small, sad line, as in picture 2
moods.angry: gently cross, a small reproachful frown: her thin eyebrows drawn together and tilted, the inner ends raised a little, as in picture 2 (one eyebrow over each eye, drawn as a single thin, faint line, the old eyebrow lines gone); the eyes slightly narrowed, glancing a little aside; the lips pressed into a small pout, as in picture 2
moods.surprised: surprised, a soft 'oh my': her thin eyebrows raised high and arched, as in picture 2 (one eyebrow over each eye, drawn as a single thin, faint line, the old eyebrow lines gone); the eyes opened wider and rounder, as in picture 2; the lips parted in a small round 'o'
moods.shy: flustered and shy: a soft pink blush on the cheeks just below the eyes, the eyes glancing aside, the lips parted a little, as in picture 2

happy.words: Her eyes stay softly closed in smiling crescents: each closed eye is one clean, dark brown lash line with a single soft eyelid crease above it; the skin above the lashes is clean and plain, with no faint lines, smudges or traces of an open eye, and no white highlight or glint on the lashes; the smile and everything else stay exactly as they are.

surprised.words: Her lips are almost closed, parted only in a tiny round opening, smaller than her iris, as in picture 2: a soft, small upper lip and a tiny dark gap; no teeth, no tongue showing; the rest of the face, her eyes and eyebrows stay exactly as they are.

frames.blink: Close her eyes as in a blink: the upper eyelids down and the lashes curved, keeping her expression.
frames.talk: Part her lips only a little, as in the middle of a soft word, keeping her expression: a small, gentle opening, no tongue showing.

blink.words: Close her eyes as in a blink: the upper eyelids down and the lashes curved, one clean eyelid line above each closed eye and nothing else above it, keeping her expression.

talk.words: Her lips parted only slightly, as when speaking softly with a gentle smile: a narrow open mouth across the same width as her smile now, its corners exactly where her smile's corners are; the upper lip follows the smile's curve, a narrow dark gap and a soft lower lip below it; no tongue.

Her eyes stay closed in smiling crescents.

Part her lips as in the middle of a quiet word, as in picture 2 but smaller: a small open mouth across the same width as her mouth now, the corners a little down, keeping her sad expression; no tongue.
Part her lips as in the middle of a word, as in picture 2 but smaller: a small open mouth across the same width as her pout now, keeping her cross expression; no tongue.
Open her small round mouth only a little more, as in the middle of a word: still a small 'o', only a little bigger than now, much smaller than picture 2's mouth; no tongue.
Part her lips as in the middle of a shy word, as in picture 2 but smaller: a small open mouth across the same width as her mouth now, keeping her flustered expression and blush; no tongue.

negative: deformed face, extra eyes, extra eyebrows, glasses, text, watermark
framesNote: every talk opens the mood's own mouth across its own width, so it opens and closes rather than turning from a wide smile into a small oval (the user: one big, one small looks wrong); the sad, cross, shy and surprised ones drawn with the sheet's speaking face (cell 12) as picture 2, the smiles without it (with it they opened far too wide); happy has no blink, and the other blinks are the neutral's shut eyes (a sad blink the model drew left the iris showing)
happyNote: the user's choice: her happy face a graceful closed-mouth smile, not the sheet's open laugh; seed 11 of fourteen closed both eyes, and a second pass over both eyes (seed 2 of eight) cleared the old open eye's traces above the lashes and the highlights' glints

moodKeepAlso.angry: the veil and its gold ornament, and exactly one thin, faint eyebrow over each eye with no second line above or below it
moodKeepAlso.surprised: the veil and its gold ornament, and exactly one thin, faint eyebrow over each eye with no second line above or below it

ornamentNote: the veil's gold ornament came out an irregular lump (the sheet's own was a loose four-armed cross). Its shape was mended in place (a five-petal flower, the top petal longer, its pale warm gold and the angle it lies at kept) and two stray leaves taken off; the top petal still leaned left. The other four petals fix the plane the flower lies in (an affine map, fitted within a pixel); in that plane the top petal points at 61 degrees, not 72. So the flower was designed in that plane (ornament/D-fit2.png, tools in the session scratchpad: rounded petals, the top one 1.28 times as long, every petal lit from the upper left, the colours sampled from the drawn flower, a narrow white rim) and the model drew it on the clean veil with the design as picture 2 (seed 7 of eight, the one whose petals keep the plane), then a light pass (0.45, seed 3) with the accepted flower as picture 2 brought back its warm gold and shiny centre. Rotating one petal five times was tried and looked pasted on: its light turned with it and it lay in no plane (the user). The same pixels laid into every frame (the ornament is outside every face region); drafts in game_pic/ilse/ornament/
